[S0026] Our drive savings continued to build sequentially and we achieved $600 million of savings in the quarter. [S0027] Taken together, these two factors enabled us to achieve 12% adjusted operating income growth compared to last year. [S0028] At Federal Express Corporation, we delivered strong year-over-year results with adjusted operating income up 17% despite significant headwinds from the expiration of the United States Postal Service contract and severe weather events. [S0029] Weakness in the industrial economy continued to pressure our higher margin B2B volumes. [S0030] Similar to last quarter, this dynamic was most pronounced at freight, where fewer shipments and lower weights continued to negatively affect our results, albeit to a lesser extent than last quarter. [S0031] Considering our B2B mix, we are well positioned to capture strong incremental flow through when the industrial economy recovers. [S0032] The current environment, however, is adding uncertainty to demand. [S0033] We continue to work closely with our customers to help them adapt to this evolving market. [S0034] Our flexible and unmatched global network, digital tools, and data ecosystem enable us to quickly support our customers' needs. [S0035] With our vast data on cross-border trade, we are uniquely positioned to create more value for our customers as they navigate change. [S0036] This includes providing a streamlined clearance experience for customers while helping them comply with regulatory requirements. [S0037] And through our automated processes, we can clear packages more quickly better address improperly filed paperwork, and reduce manual work to respond rapidly to our customers' needs while improving our operating efficiency. [S0038] As a reminder, in terms of our revenues split by geography, we serve an extremely diversified customer base across the more than 220 countries and territories. [S0039] To put some numbers around this, Taking our FY25 revenue through the third quarter, nearly 75% comes from our U.S. domestic services. [S0042] against this backdrop we remain focused on what we can control first q3 drive savings continue to ramp and were in line with our expectations we expect to achieve our incremental target of 2.2 billion dollars for fy25 and our total of 4 billion dollars of our fy23 baseline second We are creating a more flexible, efficient and intelligent network. [S0043] As planned, we resumed Network 2.0 conversions following peak. [S0044] We have optimized five US stations since the beginning of the calendar year and expect to optimize 45 more in Q4. [S0045] We are on track to complete the rollout in Canada by the end of April. [S0046] By the end of FY25, about 12% of our average daily global volume will flow through Network 2.0 optimized facilities. [S0047] Third, Tricolor is driving better asset utilization as we improve aircraft density and better leverage our surface network. [S0048] We have a broad range of KPIs that we are tracking to measure our progress. [S0049] We're especially pleased that on a year-over-year basis, Payloads across our air network are up 9%, with a 5% improvement in density. [S0050] This is a key objective of our tricolor operating model. [S0051] Importantly, our progress is leading to positive flow-through on revenue growth from international export freight. [S0052] Fourth, our planned transition away from the U.S. Postal Service contract is going well. [S0053] and we are continuing to remove costs associated with the expired contract. [S0054] Fifth, our freight separation work is underway. [S0055] John will share more details shortly. [S0056] And lastly, we are providing our customers with the best value proposition in the industry. [S0057] FedEx Ground and FedEx Home Delivery are faster to more locations than UPS Ground. [S0058] As we look to the fourth quarter, In light of the uncertain demand environment and higher than previously expected inflationary pressures on our cost base, we are lowering our FY25 adjusted EPS outlook to $18 to $18.60. [S0059] John will provide more color on the underlying assumptions. [S0060] I'm excited about our transformation progress as we continue to integrate our networks, reduce our cost to serve, and enable better performance. [S0061] Technology remains a key facilitator of our transformation. [S0062] Last quarter, I shared details on the encouraging improvement we are seeing in Europe. [S0063] That trend continued in Q3 with our simplified technology platform driving both operational efficiency and a better experience for our customers. [S0064] This is also leading to the best European service levels we have seen in years, which is driving profitable share growth. [S0065] We remain on track to achieve the $600 million in total drive savings from Europe by the end of this fiscal year. [S0066] In support of our network transformation, last month we acquired RouteSmart Technologies, a global leader in route optimization solutions. [S0067] This acquisition allows us to bring in-house a dynamic route mapping solution with the best in class algorithm. [S0068] Our legacy ground business has used this technology with great success, and we are now rolling it out globally. [S0069] This will be an important enabler for both Network 2.0 and our global network transformation, helping our team members to work safer and smarter. [S0070] In closing, I'm proud of the team for their continued success. [S0071] We navigated many headwinds in this third quarter, including a volatile demand environment, the postal service contract expiration, severe weather events, and inflation. [S0072] Yet, we still delivered 60 basis points of adjusted operating margin expansion and a 12% improvement in adjusted operating income. [S0073] Looking ahead, I'm confident that our transformation initiatives such as DRIVE, Network 2.0, and Tricolor will create long-term value for our stakeholders. [S0074] Now, let me turn the call over to Bree.

[P003] [S0075] Bri Carreri [635]: Thank you, Raj. [S0076] First, I also want to thank our team for a very successful peak. [S0077] On Cyber Monday, we picked up nearly 24 million packages in the United States. [S0078] That's nearly 70% more than we pick up in the U.S. on an average day. [S0079] And given the compressed timeline, we handled more packages per day year over year this peak season. [S0080] Well, of course, continuing to deliver the purple promise for all our customers. [S0081] While demand during peak exceeded our expectations, post-peak trends were largely consistent with the market weakness of recent quarters. [S0082] Consolidated revenue increased 2%, driven by higher volume at Federal Express, partially offset by freight. [S0083] The weak industrial economy continued to weigh on our global priority volumes in our LTL business. [S0084] Against this backdrop, we continued to focus on profitable share growth. [S0085] As we closed out calendar year 24, we took profitable share in the U.S. domestic and in international parcel, and also, because of our tri-color strategy, we grew profitable global air freight share. [S0086] Looking at each segment on a year-over-year basis, at Federal Express, revenue increased 3%, driven by increased volume in our deferred services. [S0087] At freight, lower volumes, fuel surcharges, and weight per shipment pressured our top line performance. [S0088] This led to a 5% revenue decline. [S0089] Overall volume trends improved in the quarter to our highest year-over-year average daily volume growth since Q4 of fiscal year 21, led by 5% growth in Federal Express package volumes. [S0090] Our volume growth was driven by deferred services and the timing benefit of Cyber Week. [S0091] And while LTL volumes were pressured, the rate of decline in average daily shipments improved compared to Q2. [S0092] Across U.S. domestic express services, volumes increased slightly, with growth in deferred services partially offset by decline in priority volume. [S0093] Ground volumes increased 7%, supported both by B2B and B2C growth. [S0094] International export package volumes increased 8% in the quarter due to continued growth in the international economy. [S0095] With air freight, average daily pounds increased 3% for international priority freight. [S0096] As we shared last quarter, the growth here is tied directly to our tri-color strategy to grow profitably in the global air freight market. [S0099] And at FedEx Freight, the soft industrial economy led to a 5% decline in average daily shipments and a 3% decline in weight per shipment. [S0100] We remain focused on quality growth amid a competitive but rational pricing environment. [S0101] I am encouraged by recent pricing trends. [S0102] Holiday demand surcharges supported our results, and consistent with historical trends, we are seeing a strong capture rate on the 5.9% GRI implemented this past January. [S0103] At Federal Express, U.S. domestic package yield was flat year over year, as higher U.S. Express overnight package, ground commercial, and home delivery yield was offset by lower ground economy yield. [S0104] Similar to last quarter, and in line with our expectations, international export package yield declined, driven by international economy, partially offset by an 8% yield increase for international priority. [S0105] At FedEx Freight, revenue per shipment declined 1% due to lower fuel surcharge revenue and lower weight per shipment. [S0106] However, revenue per hundredweight increased 2%, a testament to our focus on revenue quality in the industry's continued pricing discipline. [S0107] As we look ahead, we expect FY25 revenue to be flat to down slightly versus last year. [S0108] For the fourth quarter, this implies essentially flat revenue at Federal Express, driven primarily by continued volume growth and deferred service offerings, partially offset by one fewer operating day. [S0109] At freight, we expect a continued revenue decline on a year-over-year basis in Q4, but also expect the Q4 decline to moderate sequentially. [S0110] Last quarter, I shared with you the framework for our commercial priorities. [S0111] B2B growth, including healthcare and automotive, a focus on U.S. domestic e-commerce, profitable growth and global air freight segment, and of course, we want to accelerate profitable growth in Europe. [S0112] I am very pleased to report that we've had progress across all of our priorities. [S0113] A few highlights from the quarter. [S0114] We continue to build unique capabilities for our high margin healthcare vertical. [S0115] For example, we are taking our established returns platform and using that technology for customers that require recurring collaborative shipments with their business partners or vendors. [S0116] This has varied use cases across industries, including lab shipments between medical providers. [S0117] This process enables a simpler shipping process with more visibility, allowing shipment recipients to staff more appropriately and efficiently. [S0118] Due to the hard work of our team and our compelling healthcare value proposition, we are onboarding nearly $400 million in new annualized healthcare revenue over the next 90 days. [S0119] Our advanced capabilities help to track this new business with three quarters of this business tied to bundled customers who are using in the FedEx surround suite. [S0120] As a result of these wins, we will exit FY25 with approximately 9 billion in healthcare revenue. [S0121] Additionally, we further expanded FedEx surround monitoring and intervention, and now we offer this solution in over 40 countries. [S0122] Surround's real-time AI-powered dashboard gives customers enhanced visibility and control over their shipments, which is especially helpful for customers transporting high-value or sensitive goods. [S0123] With 90% of the market's incremental parcel growth expected to come from e-commerce, we continue to refine how we profitably serve this market. [S0124] Based on demand from our largest customers, we have expanded our Sunday residential coverage to nearly two-thirds of the U.S. population, up from 50% previously. [S0125] We have already received incremental commitments of more than half a million packages per week from existing customers tied to our Sunday delivery capabilities. [S0126] This change is enabling us to better utilize our existing assets without adding capacity while meeting the needs of our customers. [S0127] As a result, we expect this incremental coverage to be profit accretive in Q1 of fiscal year 26. [S0128] We will continue to lean into these key strategies as we target profitable growth in the quarters and years ahead. [S0129] And with that, I will turn it over to John.

[S0174] And including our dividend, we're on track to return $3.8 billion to shareholders in FY25. [S0175] Capital expenditures were $997 million, and our planned FY25 CapEx is now down to $4.9 billion, a $300 million decline compared to last year's $5.2 billion, supporting strong free cash flow and shareholder returns. [S0176] From a fleet standpoint, we recently reached agreements to purchase eight new Boeing 777 freighter aircraft and two used 777 freighters which will be phased in during calendar years 26 and 27. [S0177] These modern and fuel-efficient aircraft were purchased at attractive prices and will help us manage our fleet for the long term while still upholding our FY26 commitment to approximately $1 billion of aircraft CapEx. [S0178] Given that these new planes are highly efficient and will retire our older, more maintenance-intensive fleet over time, I'm confident that aircraft capex in the immediate years beyond FY26 will remain in the area of $1 billion. [S0179] We've continued to manage and rationalize the size of our jet fleet, including retiring some of our older aircraft over the last several years.
